cases.name: Melody Marie Hoffman
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Melody, true to her name, loved all kinds of music. Melody enjoyed her time at Liberty High School and Kirkwood Community College, where she met many good friends. She loved swimming, camping, concerts, and being involved in scouting. She volunteered at the Linn County Animal Shelter and looked forward to volunteering more. Her love for animals ran deep. Every chance she had to donate blood she took it. She loved to hear about the impact her donation made. She was the most loving and caring person who would help anyone. She knew no strangers, had no fear, and loved everyone unconditionally."

She was very sweet, happy and trusting and she was very close with her mother, who described her as being curious and having no fear when she was younger. Her mother also said she loved her teachers and thrived on interactions with adults, and loved animals, kids and babies and cared about everyone.
cases.narrative:
On 2/18/2024, a woman found Melody's body face down, nude except for her underwear, dumped at Lily Lake in Amana, IA. She had postmortem X-shaped slash marks and stab wounds on her back, a cut mark to her finger, bruises on her face, and a ligature mark on her neck.

Louisma told authorities that he and Van Patten bound Hoffman’s wrists with duct tape when they were at Morgan Creek Park, before putting her in the trunk of his car and driving to Lily Lake in Iowa County, IA. The two allegedly beat her while she begged for them to let her go, the affidavit says, before leaving her to die at the pond. Associate State Medical Examiner Dr. Kelly Kruse testified that the main cause of death for Hoffman was strangulation by something other than hands Rope found in Louisma’s car matches paracord found in Van Patten's house that investigators believe was used to strangle Hoffman. Hoffman also suffered blunt force injuries to her head, five stab wounds, serrated knife cuts, six cutting wounds to her right hand and various abrasions and bruises on her face.

During her murder, they also tore off her clothing and a necklace which contained the cremated ashes of her deceased baby sister. She had cried out: "That's my sister's!"
